correctness.rationale: The exact projector is [[-ab,a],[b,0]] and its symmetric part has squared Frobenius norm a²b²+(a+b)²/2. Conditional on correlated denominator vectors, the coefficients are a nonsingular bivariate Gaussian pair unless |rho|=1. Joint Gaussian inverse-power integrability and a compact conditional correlation bound yield p<ell for |rho|<1; at |rho|=1 the coefficients coincide and yield p<ell/2. Classical inverse-chi moments establish the exact independent/shared squared-risk formulas; the shared Gaussian/chi density establishes its tail constant. A two-dimensional Laplace integral and explicit evaluations at ell=3,4 give the near-perfect-correlation divergence orders. The 10,731 finite exact/numerical checks of verify.py supplement rather than prove the infinite laws. Exact arithmetic, all ell>=1 and d>=max(ell+1,2), all rho∈[-1,1].

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by whether to enforce symmetry by sharing a sketch or by symmetrizing the output of independent sketches. The new sharp loss of two sketch rows in the mean-square threshold (three versus five), complete p-moment phase boundary and quantified singular three/four-row near-coupling risk identify a nontrivial numerical design issue. It concerns a natural positive normal forcing of the actual rank-one oblique DLRA map; not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere known-table recomputation, and it does not overclaim entire integrator stability.
